A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MANEC of the biliary tract is not only a rare neoplasm, but also a neoplasm with diverse differentiation, which is a challenge to pathologists.
MANEC of the biliary tract may be regarded as a neoplasm of the 'ductulo-squamous complex'.

the present tumor is an example of 'neoplastic transformation' in which the tumor cells have undergone a process similar to that of metaplasia, in which the original epithelial tissue is converted to an entirely different tissue, in the course of neoplastic progression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the differential diagnosis of a gallbladder polyp, a large polyp with a lobulated surface should always be considered a possible malignant tumor.
MANEC of the pancreas and biliary tract should be considered in the differential diagnosis of a tumor showing diverse differentiation.

the presence of a mixed pattern in a neoplasm should not be regarded as a mere combination of different neoplasms, but rather, should prompt a search for the possibility of a common precursor cell, and the presence of a common precursor may be inferred by the observation of a morphological transition between different components.
